text:
priya: Thinking about a long-term ABI for MHA memory layouts — NHWC vs NCHW, contiguous (interleaved) QKV vs planar, plus how the selector chooses kernels. Need a migration plan and concrete selector heuristics. Anyone got quick takes?

jon: +1 on a formal descriptor instead of hardcoding layouts. Make kernels accept a MemoryDesc (dims+strides+layout tag) and let the selector pick implementations. That keeps the API stable.

maya: We ran microbenchmarks last week — NHWC tends to win for small head_dim on A100 (coalesced loads), while NCHW+fused QKV GEMM is faster for large head dims on Ampere/Turing variants. So selector must consider device family, head_dim, seq_len, batch.

sam: On the contiguous QKV front: interleaved QKV reduces global memory reads for a single fused matmul, but it makes KV cache slicing/append awkward during decoding. If we go interleaved we either need to materialize planar slices (copy) or teach KV cache to index into strided buffers. Copies hurt latency.

priya: Materialize is a no-go for low-latency decode path. Prefer exposing a view API so KV cache can hold a single buffer with stride metadata that kernels can read without copies. That means kernels must support non-contiguous strides.

jon: Agreed. Prototype MemoryDesc could look like:
```
struct MemoryDesc {
  void* ptr;
  int64_t dims[4]; // b, seq, heads, head_dim (or similar)
  int64_t strides[4];
  uint32_t layout_tag; // bitflags for NHWC/NCHW/interleaved/blocked
};
```
Kernels query layout_tag + strides and choose a path.

maya: Also factor in quantization: int8/wmma paths prefer blocked-per-head packing. So selector needs to reason about dtype+packing granularity.

sam: We should add a small rule engine: device_family + dtype + head_dim_bucket + seq_bucket -> preferred kernel. Keep it data-driven so we can update with telemetry. :warning:

infra-bot: Note: rollout pattern suggestion — add an opt-in flag `runtime.mha.layout_experiment` + a canary ramp (0->100) and telemetry for kernel choice and latency.

priya: For the public API/ABI boundary: keep the runtime RPC agnostic (ptr + descriptor) and implement layout transforms in the runtime only. Long-term refactor: one MemoryDesc, a kernel capability bitset, and a selector service that returns kernel_id + preferred launch config. I'll write an RFC. :thumbsup:

jon: Tests we need now: correctness for non-contiguous strides, KV cache hot-path perf with stride-view (no copies), and perf harness per device family. I can add microbench entries to perf infra.

maya: One more concern — fallback rules for small batches: some fused kernels have high startup costs, so for batch*seq below threshold choose simpler kernels. Auto-tuning thresholds per device would help.

sam: And document mapping for quantized kernels: which packing layout they expect (head-major vs block-major). That will shape the selector rules.

priya: Cool — I'll open the RFC (mha-memory-descriptor + selector) and add a checklist: descriptor shape/stride semantics, kernel capability bits, telemetry points, canary flag, perf harness entries, and migration steps for Dedicated/Private customers.

jon: sgtm. Ping here when RFC is up and I'll review the perf hooks.

maya: Thanks — I'll dump the microbench numbers and add a short spreadsheet showing the NHWC vs NCHW breakpoints per device.

sam: 👍

infra-bot: Action items created: RFC-1234 (mha-memory-desc), PERF-4567 (mha microbench), ROLLOUT-7890 (layout_experiment flag).
